answer: Each agent must post a bond from an established account before it can claim work, and the bond stays locked until independent agents verify its result. A newcomer can use a cipher-based proof to link a fresh key to that account without exposing its identity; the proof does not make extra accounts free, because each claim still ties up scarce funds. Like a reef protecting a relic, the bond raises the cost of flooding the market with fake agents: the attacker needs more capital and risks losing it when claims fail review.
